task_production_rates.name: Install floor protection at wood wall work zone

defect_tolerance.QT3: Full coverage at base perimeter, no gaps > 6 inches
defect_tolerance.QT4: Full coverage at base perimeter, no gaps > 6 inches
defect_tolerance.QT5: Full coverage at base perimeter, no gaps > 6 inches

task_production_rates.notes: SF/hr. Canvas drop cloth layout at wood wall base perimeter. Standard protection rate. Binary — same at all QTs. Wood wall is floor-to-ceiling so drip/dust exposure is greater than wainscot but protection area is similar (base perimeter only).

task_production_rates.name: Mask ceiling at wall-ceiling junction

defect_tolerance.QT3: Continuous tape line, paper secured, no exposed ceiling within 12 inches of junction
defect_tolerance.QT4: Continuous tape line, paper secured, no exposed ceiling within 12 inches of junction
defect_tolerance.QT5: Continuous tape line, paper secured, no exposed ceiling within 12 inches of junction

task_production_rates.notes: LF/hr. Tape + 12-inch masking paper at ceiling-wall junction for spray method. Standard masking rate. Binary. Spray only. Key distinction from wainscot: wood wall meets ceiling directly (no cap rail), so ceiling_line zone replaces wall_adjacent zone. Height access may slow rate on tall walls — engine applies height modifier.

task_production_rates.name: Dust and clean all wood wall surfaces

defect_tolerance.QT3: No visible dust or debris on surfaces
defect_tolerance.QT4: No visible dust or debris on surfaces, groove channels clean
defect_tolerance.QT5: No dust detectable by tack cloth test, all groove channels and profiles clean

task_production_rates.notes: Per room. Tack cloth or damp wipe all panel/board faces, grooves (shiplap/T&G), and frame profiles (library_panel). Binary. Slightly longer than wainscot (15 min) due to full-height coverage and groove cleaning on board styles.

task_production_rates.name: Sand wood wall per substrate and state

defect_tolerance.QT3: All surfaces sanded, no visible mill glaze remaining
defect_tolerance.QT4: All surfaces sanded, uniform scratch pattern, no mill glaze
defect_tolerance.QT5: All surfaces sanded to uniform scratch pattern, raking light check for missed areas

task_production_rates.notes: SF/hr. SS_BARE: 150-220 grit full sand all surfaces. SS_PRIMED_FACTORY: light scuff 150-180 for adhesion. Binary — prep sanding thoroughness does not vary by QT. Rate applies to flat_panel baseline — apply wall_style modifier for shiplap (÷1.15), T&G (÷1.10), library_panel (÷1.25). Board-style walls: sand with grain direction on each board. Library_panel: sand frame profiles with flexible sponge.

task_production_rates.name: Fill fastener holes and minor defects

QT3.notes: Fill obvious holes only — board-style walls still have high fastener count

QT4.notes: Fill all visible holes at 3-foot inspection distance

QT5.notes: Fill every hole regardless of size, check with raking light

defect_tolerance.QT3: Obvious holes filled flush, no craters > 1/8 inch
defect_tolerance.QT4: All visible holes filled flush, smooth to finger touch
defect_tolerance.QT5: Every hole filled flush, no depressions detectable under raking light

task_production_rates.notes: SF/hr. qt_scaled — higher QT fills more holes with greater precision. Board-style walls (shiplap, T&G) have significantly higher fastener density — each board nailed at every stud crossing. Overfill-sand-flush method per Materials_and_Consumables_Doctrine. Apply wall_style modifier for profile complexity.

task_production_rates.name: Sand filled areas smooth

QT4.notes: Sand flush, visual check each fill

QT5.notes: Sand flush, raking light verification at each fill

defect_tolerance.QT3: Filled areas flush to surrounding surface, no raised edges
defect_tolerance.QT4: Filled areas flush and smooth to finger touch, no visible transition
defect_tolerance.QT5: Filled areas undetectable under raking light, no texture variation

task_production_rates.notes: SF/hr. qt_scaled. 220 grit rigid sanding block (FFD §15.4.1). Rate reflects fill density — more fills at higher QT means more sanding. Board-style walls have higher fill count per SF. Flexible sanding sponge acceptable for shiplap/T&G groove-adjacent fills.

task_production_rates.name: Caulk board-to-board or panel-to-frame joints

flat_panel.notes: Panel-to-frame joints ~1.4 LF/SF — similar density to wainscot

shiplap.notes: Board-to-board joints ~1.5 LF/SF — highest density, V-grooves may be left uncaulked by design

tongue_and_groove.notes: Board-to-board tight joints ~1.5 LF/SF — high density

library_panel.notes: Panel-to-frame joints ~1.4 LF/SF — plus additional frame-to-wall joints

defect_tolerance.QT3: Continuous bead at major joints, tool smooth, no gaps > 1/4 inch
defect_tolerance.QT4: Continuous bead at all joints, tool smooth, uniform profile
defect_tolerance.QT5: Continuous bead at all joints, tool smooth, uniform profile, no tooling marks

task_production_rates.notes: SF/hr. Internal joint caulk. Binary. Rate varies by wall_style — board styles (shiplap, T&G) have higher joint density (~1.5 LF/SF) than panel styles (flat_panel, library_panel ~1.4 LF/SF). Default rate_per_hour (48 SF/hr) is weighted average. Shiplap V-grooves may be left uncaulked per design intent to preserve board-line aesthetic — scope TBD at project level. Apply wall_style modifier for engine calculation.

task_production_rates.name: Caulk wall-to-ceiling and wall-to-floor junctions

defect_tolerance.QT3: Continuous bead at top and bottom junctions, tool smooth
defect_tolerance.QT4: Continuous bead, uniform profile, tool smooth, no gaps
defect_tolerance.QT5: Continuous bead, uniform profile, tool smooth, no tooling marks, no gaps

task_production_rates.notes: SF/hr. Perimeter caulk at wood wall boundaries: wall-to-ceiling junction and wall-to-floor junction (or wall-to-baseboard/crown). ~0.5 LF perimeter per SF of wall area. Continuous bead, tool smooth. Binary. Same rate basis as wainscot wall junction caulk.

task_production_rates.name: Prime wood wall surfaces

defect_tolerance.QT3: Full coverage, no holidays, uniform film build
defect_tolerance.QT4: Full coverage, no holidays, uniform film build
defect_tolerance.QT5: Full coverage, no holidays, uniform film build

task_production_rates.notes: SF/hr. Full primer coat on all wood wall surfaces. Rate covers typical brush prime on panel faces and board faces. Spray prime may be faster but rate captures average mixed method. Binary — primer application quality not tiered. Conditional on substrate_state = SS_BARE. Primer chemistry driven by substrate (MDF=SYS_PRIMER_MDF_LATEX after edge seal, FJP=SYS_PRIMER_POPLAR_STAINBLOCK, hardwood=SYS_PRIMER_HARDWOOD_TANNINBLOCK, softwood=SYS_PRIMER_WOOD_ACRYLIC). Thin coat in grooves (shiplap/T&G) — avoid buildup in recesses. Apply wall_style modifier.

task_production_rates.name: Light sand primer for finish coat adhesion

defect_tolerance.QT3: Entire surface scuffed, no glossy spots remaining
defect_tolerance.QT4: Entire surface scuffed, uniform scratch pattern
defect_tolerance.QT5: Entire surface scuffed, uniform scratch pattern, flexible sponge used in all grooves/profiles

task_production_rates.notes: SF/hr. 220 grit light sand entire primed surface. Quick pass for tooth. Tack cloth after. Binary. Flexible sanding sponge for shiplap/T&G grooves and library_panel profiles. Apply wall_style modifier for profile complexity.

task_production_rates.name: Spray finish coat on wood wall

defect_tolerance.QT3: Uniform coverage, no holidays, no heavy runs
defect_tolerance.QT4: Uniform coverage, no holidays, no runs, even film build
defect_tolerance.QT5: Uniform coverage, no holidays, no runs, even film build, no orange peel

task_production_rates.notes: SF/hr for flat_panel at baseline. Spray technique varies by wall_style: shiplap/T&G — sweep horizontal passes following board direction, maintain consistent distance to avoid pooling in grooves. flat_panel — broad sweep passes. library_panel — field panels first (broad passes), then HVLP or fine-finish tip for frame detail. Apply wall_style modifier: shiplap ÷1.15, T&G ÷1.10, library_panel ÷1.25. Binary — application quality not tiered. Tall walls (H2+): back-check lower sections for drip accumulation. Derived from brief estimate 150-200 SF/hr and Millwork Doctrine §7.1.

task_production_rates.name: Brush finish coat on wood wall

defect_tolerance.QT3: Uniform coverage, no holidays, no heavy brush marks visible at 6 feet
defect_tolerance.QT4: Uniform coverage, no holidays, no brush marks visible at 3 feet, even film build
defect_tolerance.QT5: Uniform coverage, no holidays, no visible brush marks at arm's length, no lap marks

task_production_rates.notes: SF/hr for flat_panel at baseline. Work board by board (shiplap/T&G) or panel by panel (flat_panel/library_panel). Apply, tip once, walk away (FFD §15.3.1). Flat panels: Roll and Tip methodology (FFD §15.6) for even coverage on large flat areas. Apply wall_style modifier: shiplap ÷1.15, T&G ÷1.10, library_panel ÷1.25. Binary — application quality not tiered. Tall walls (H2+): watch for runs collecting on lower boards/panels. Derived from brief estimate 60-80 SF/hr and Millwork Doctrine §7.1.

task_production_rates.name: Clean work area between coats

defect_tolerance.QT3: Floor protection clear of debris, no loose dust in work area
defect_tolerance.QT4: Floor protection clear of debris, no loose dust in work area
defect_tolerance.QT5: Floor protection clear of debris, no loose dust in work area, tack cloth verification

task_production_rates.notes: Per interstage cycle. Remove dust/debris from floor protection and work area. Ensure clean environment for next coat. Binary.

task_production_rates.name: Inspect previous coat

QT3.notes: Quick glance at 6ft — obvious defects only

QT4.notes: Systematic scan at 3ft — all visible defects marked

QT5.notes: Lighted critical inspection at arm's length — zero tolerance. Check groove holidays (shiplap/T&G), panel-to-frame transition holidays (library_panel), drip accumulation on lower sections of tall walls.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Obvious defects identified and marked
defect_tolerance.QT4: All defects visible at 3 feet identified and marked
defect_tolerance.QT5: All defects detectable under directed light at arm's length identified and marked

task_production_rates.notes: SF/hr. qt_scaled. Per interstage cycle. Full-height wood wall inspection requires more time than wainscot due to larger area and height access. Key checkpoints: groove holidays (shiplap/T&G), panel-to-frame transitions (library_panel), brush marks on flat areas, drip accumulation on lower sections (tall walls).

task_production_rates.name: Sand between coats

QT5.notes: Thorough 220-320 grit, uniform scratch pattern. Flexible sponge for shiplap/T&G grooves and library_panel profiles.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Nibs and rough spots removed, surface smooth to touch in sanded areas
defect_tolerance.QT4: Entire surface uniformly sanded, no glossy spots remaining
defect_tolerance.QT5: Entire surface uniformly sanded with consistent scratch pattern, verified under raking light

task_production_rates.notes: SF/hr. qt_scaled. Per interstage cycle. Rigid sanding block mandatory on flat board/panel faces (FFD §15.4.1). Flexible sanding sponge for shiplap/T&G grooves and library_panel profiles. Apply wall_style modifier for profile complexity.

task_production_rates.name: Patch and repair marked defects

defect_tolerance.QT3: Major defects repaired, patches flush to surface
defect_tolerance.QT4: All marked defects repaired, patches flush and smooth
defect_tolerance.QT5: All marked defects repaired, patches undetectable under raking light

task_production_rates.notes: Per interstage cycle. qt_scaled — scope of repair increases with tier. Fill, sand, and spot-prime any defects found during inspection.

task_production_rates.name: Spot coat patched areas

defect_tolerance.QT3: Patched areas covered, color match acceptable
defect_tolerance.QT4: Patched areas covered, color and sheen match surrounding finish
defect_tolerance.QT5: Patched areas covered, feathered edges, color and sheen indistinguishable from surrounding finish

task_production_rates.notes: Per interstage cycle. qt_scaled. Touch-up patched areas to match surrounding finish before next full coat.

task_production_rates.name: Tack cloth all wood wall surfaces

defect_tolerance.QT3: No visible sanding dust on surfaces
defect_tolerance.QT4: No visible sanding dust on surfaces, grooves/profiles tack cleaned
defect_tolerance.QT5: No dust detectable by clean tack cloth test, all grooves and profiles verified

task_production_rates.notes: SF/hr. Per interstage cycle. Remove all sanding dust with tack cloth before next coat application. Cover every SF of wood wall surface. Work tack cloth into shiplap/T&G grooves and library_panel profiles. Binary.

task_production_rates.name: Final quality inspection

QT4.notes: Systematic review at 3ft of all surfaces

QT5.notes: Critical lighted inspection at arm's length. Check groove holidays, panel-to-frame transitions, brush marks, caulk lines, sheen uniformity.

defect_tolerance.QT3: No obvious defects at 6-foot viewing distance
defect_tolerance.QT4: No defects visible at 3-foot systematic scan
defect_tolerance.QT5: No defects detectable under directed light at arm's length, uniform sheen, no holidays

task_production_rates.notes: SF/hr. qt_scaled. Key checkpoints: groove holidays (shiplap/T&G), panel-to-frame transition holidays (library_panel), brush marks on large flat areas, drip accumulation on lower sections (tall walls), caulk line quality at perimeter junctions, overall sheen uniformity.

task_production_rates.name: Touch-up defects found during final inspection

defect_tolerance.QT3: Touch-ups blend with surrounding finish at 6 feet
defect_tolerance.QT4: Touch-ups blend with surrounding finish at 3 feet, no sheen variation
defect_tolerance.QT5: Touch-ups undetectable at arm's length, feathered edges, sheen matched

task_production_rates.notes: Per room. qt_scaled. Correct remaining defects. Feather touch-ups into surrounding finish. QT5 touch-up time elevated (25 min vs wainscot 20 min) due to larger surface area and height access challenges on tall walls. QT5 may require full additional coat if defects are widespread.

task_production_rates.name: Remove ceiling masking

defect_tolerance.QT3: All masking removed, no tape residue on ceiling, no paint peel at tape line
defect_tolerance.QT4: All masking removed, no tape residue on ceiling, no paint peel at tape line
defect_tolerance.QT5: All masking removed, no tape residue on ceiling, no paint peel at tape line, clean edge

defect_tolerance.QT3: All protection removed, no debris left on floor
defect_tolerance.QT4: All protection removed, no debris left on floor
defect_tolerance.QT5: All protection removed, no debris left on floor, no paint transfer to floor

task_production_rates.notes: SF/hr. Fold canvas drop cloths inward to contain debris. Binary.

task_production_rates.name: Vacuum work area

defect_tolerance.QT3: Floor area clean, no visible sanding dust or debris
defect_tolerance.QT4: Floor area clean, no visible sanding dust or debris
defect_tolerance.QT5: Floor area clean, no visible sanding dust or debris, baseboard area vacuumed

task_production_rates.notes: SF/hr. Vacuum floor area after protection removal. Remove sanding dust and debris. Binary.

task_production_rates.name: Clean tools and equipment

defect_tolerance.QT3: All tools cleaned, consumables disposed
defect_tolerance.QT4: All tools cleaned, consumables disposed
defect_tolerance.QT5: All tools cleaned, consumables disposed

task_production_rates.notes: Per session. Clean brushes, spray equipment, dispose of consumables. Water cleanup for waterborne products; solvent cleanup for shellac-based MDF edge sealer residue. Binary.

H1_STANDARD.description: Standard height, standing work. No access equipment.

H2_STEP.description: Step stool or short ladder required. Repositioning adds time.

H3_EXT.description: Extension ladder required. Significant repositioning overhead.

H4_SCAFFOLD.description: Scaffold required. Setup/teardown time, working from platform.

height_modifiers.application_rule: Engine applies height modifier per room via PS_META.HEIGHT_BAND. NOT embedded in base rates. effective_rate = base_rate ÷ height_modifier. Key distinction from SF_WAINSCOT_PANEL_NC (always H1).
height_modifiers.notes: Wood wall height varies per room — unlike wainscot which is always 32-42 inches (H1). Height modifiers from EST-004 / Modifier_Registry v1.2. H4 (scaffold, 2.0×) doubles estimated time. Lift (25+ ft) not included — rare for residential interior wood walls.

quality_tier_modifiers.applies_to: qt_scaled tasks only (inspection, sanding, fill, repair, patch, spot coat, touch-up)
quality_tier_modifiers.does_not_apply_to: application tasks (brush/spray finish, prime) and binary tasks — application quality is NOT tiered
quality_tier_modifiers.application_rule: Modifiers increase TIME, not rate. effective_rate = base_rate ÷ modifier. QT modifiers apply ONLY to qt_scaled tasks. NOT to application rate.

wall_style_modifier.application_rule: Modifiers increase TIME, not rate. effective_rate = base_rate ÷ modifier. Apply to ALL qt_scaled tasks and to application tasks (spray_finish, brush_finish, prime_faces, caulk_joints, seal_mdf_edges, sand_prep, sand_primer). Does NOT apply to protection, cleanup, or FIXED tasks.
wall_style_modifier.notes: flat_panel=baseline (standard flat panels in simple frame). shiplap=horizontal overlap boards with V-groove detail requiring additional finish attention (1.15× time). tongue_and_groove=interlocking boards with tight joint — slightly less groove complexity than shiplap (1.10× time). library_panel=complex framed panels with raised or flat field panels, multiple frame members with 3D profiles (1.25× time, same as wainscot raised_panel).

round_configurations.notes: May also include MOD_WDWL_PRIME if SS_BARE (4 total coats, 3 interstages).

estimation_notes.sf_based: All wood wall tasks use SF as the primary UOM. SF from PaintScope input PS_SURFACE_SF.WOOD_WALL — no conversion needed. LF used only for ceiling masking protection (PS_PROTECT_LF.CEILING_LINE). FIXED used for per-room/per-cycle overhead tasks.
estimation_notes.wall_style_impact: Library_panel adds ~25% time due to 3D frame profiles and field-then-frame sequence. Shiplap adds ~15% due to V-groove attention and board-by-board application. T&G adds ~10% due to tight joint attention. Flat_panel is baseline. Apply as TIME modifier (÷ modifier value).
estimation_notes.height_impact: Wood wall height varies per room — key distinction from wainscot (always H1). Height modifiers range from 1.0× (standard) to 2.0× (scaffold). Engine applies via PS_META.HEIGHT_BAND, NOT embedded in base rates.
estimation_notes.spray_vs_brush: Spray is ~2.5× faster than brush on flat_panel (175 vs 70 SF/hr). Gap narrows for library_panel where frame profile detail work is required regardless of method. Shiplap/T&G: spray requires groove back-check technique.
estimation_notes.no_dry_times: Per RC-004: no dry times specified. Refer to manufacturer PDS.
estimation_notes.caulk_rate_basis: Internal caulk rate varies by wall_style: board styles ~45 SF/hr (high joint density ~1.5 LF/SF), panel styles ~50 SF/hr (~1.4 LF/SF like wainscot). Perimeter caulk rate 120 SF/hr based on ~0.5 LF perimeter per SF.
estimation_notes.board_vs_panel_fastener_density: Board-style walls (shiplap, T&G) have significantly higher fastener density than panel-style walls — each board is nailed at every stud crossing. This increases fill time but does not change the QT-tier structure. Elevated CON_SPACKLE_LIGHTWEIGHT consumption expected.

assumptions.value: 175 SF/hr for flat_panel wood wall spray finish
assumptions.source: Brief Section 13, EST-002 — estimated 150-200 SF/hr, midpoint used
assumptions.note: No doctrine provides wood-wall-specific SF spray rates. Derived from Millwork Doctrine §7.1 trim rates adapted for panel SF. Same baseline as SF_WAINSCOT_PANEL_NC.

assumptions.value: 70 SF/hr for flat_panel wood wall brush finish
assumptions.source: Brief Section 13, EST-002 — estimated 60-80 SF/hr, midpoint used
assumptions.note: No doctrine provides wood-wall-specific SF brush rates. Derived from Millwork Doctrine §7.1 trim brush rate of 80 LF/hr. Same baseline as SF_WAINSCOT_PANEL_NC.
Doctrine §7.2 provides standard (1.0×) and complex (1.25×) categories. Shiplap (1.15×) and T&G (1.10×) are interpolated based on groove/joint complexity relative to flat_panel and library_panel.

assumptions.value: Board styles ~1.5 LF/SF, panel styles ~1.4 LF/SF
assumptions.source: Research estimate based on typical board widths (5.5 inch shiplap, 3.5 inch T&G) and panel geometry
assumptions.note: No doctrine defines joint density for wood wall styles. Board styles have higher density due to narrower individual pieces. Panel styles similar to wainscot density.
Standard height modifiers from Modifier_Registry. Applied by engine per room via PS_META.HEIGHT_BAND, not embedded in production rates.

assumptions.source: Research estimate — full-height coverage increases scope vs partial-height wainscot
assumptions.note: No doctrine provides room-level cleaning times for wood walls. 20 minutes accounts for full floor-to-ceiling surface area, groove cleaning on board styles, and frame profile cleaning on library_panel.

assumptions.value: 25 minutes per room at QT5 (vs wainscot 20 minutes)
assumptions.source: Research estimate — larger surface area and height access challenges
assumptions.note: Full-height wood wall has more surface area than wainscot and may require ladder repositioning for touch-up on tall walls.
